assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged network retrieval is a same-origin fetch of an image URL returned by the host's own SillyTavern Image Generation pipeline. The response is constrained to an image content type, capped at 16 MB, converted into a File object, and only ever used as an NPC portrait preview or attachment. The correlated 'execution sink' in the window is image decoding via Image/canvas and DOM element assignment, not evaluation of fetched content as code. No eval, Function construction, or command execution consumes network data. This data flow is proportionate to the extension's stated portrait-generation feature.
assessments.layman_explanation: The extension fetches a picture that the host app's own image generator produced, checks that it is really an image of a reasonable size, and shows it as an NPC portrait. Nothing downloaded is ever run as code. This is exactly what the feature promises in the README.

assessments.technical_explanation: The flagged line resolves the host-generated portrait URL against the current document location (with a localhost fallback for non-browser test contexts) and fetches it with same-origin credentials. The blob is validated as an image type, additionally checked against the project's portrait file validation, capped at 16 MB, sanitized into a safe filename, and used solely as the NPC portrait. The URL originates from the extension's own call into the host's image generation runtime, not from untrusted user or remote content, and nothing retrieved is executed or persisted outside the dossier state file.
assessments.layman_explanation: This code downloads the picture the host app just generated, confirms it is a valid image within a size limit, and attaches it to an NPC's profile. It only talks to the same server the app already runs on, and nothing it downloads is ever run as a program.

assessments.technical_explanation: The static scanner signal at this location corresponds to the URL-resolution code that turns the host-provided generated-image URL into an absolute address before fetching it with same-origin credentials, plus a localhost fallback base used only when no document location exists (e.g. isolated tests). The fetch is same-origin, response-validated as an image, and size-limited. No credential, token, or chat content is attached or sent, and no attacker-controlled destination is established by the supplied code.
assessments.layman_explanation: A scanner flagged the web-address handling code, but the code only turns the address of a locally generated picture into a full address so it can be downloaded and shown as a portrait. It does not contact any suspicious outside service or leak any data.
